AmuseMe turns a PDF (a research paper, a medical letter, a court opinion, a class handout or a business brief) into a reading guide where every explanation cites an exact quote. Choose a guided walkthrough, its main claims and limits, or a document map, then open any quote highlighted in the clean text or beside the original page. Read the complete document and download its text, images and processing report.

1. **Upload a PDF.** Choose how you want to read while AmuseMe processes the document. Live progress says in plain words what Muse is doing ("Muse is checking page 2 of 4"), lists every stage and shows the time elapsed. A short document takes about five minutes; a document too long for one run gets a clear message instead of a technical error.
2. **Choose a way in.** Read a short overview, follow a walkthrough, or examine the main claims, their support and their limits. Each AI-written explanation links to quotations in the uploaded paper. A document map shows which passages each step and claim cites. Older saved documents without a guide remain available in the normal reader.
3. **Check the document.** Open the quoted passage highlighted in its page text, or switch to the original page. Browse the full text, equations, tables and figures. The processing report says what Muse double-checked: problems a second review fixed, and places where Muse kept the original text. AI explanations and figure descriptions remain separate from the source.
4. **Take it with you.** Copy the complete normalized text or download a ZIP. The structured document includes its saved guide; the processing report records changes and unresolved issues.

The HTTP adapter accepts only `POST /auth/sign-in/email`, `POST /auth/sign-out`, `GET /auth/get-session`, `GET /auth/sign-in-options`, and, only when email-only sign-in is enabled, `POST /auth/sign-in/judge`. 3. Email-only sign-in is off by default and enabled only by `AMUSEME_JUDGE_SIGN_IN=true`. It is the `amuseme-judge-sign-in` Better Auth plugin endpoint, so Better Auth's origin/CSRF checks, database rate limiter, session creation and cookies apply. The body is `{ email, accessCode? }`. When `AMUSEME_JUDGE_ACCESS_CODE` is set, a missing or different code returns 401 before any lookup; the comparison does not stop early. The email is trimmed, lowercased and must be a single address of at most 254 characters, otherwise 400. An unknown email creates a user with role `user` and no credential account; a known email signs in only if that user has role `user` and no linked account. Invited password accounts and admins return 403 and never get a session this way. Request role, name and owner fields are ignored. Anyone who knows an email-only address can open that account; this deliberately trades account secrecy for frictionless judge access, so these accounts hold only their own uploads and read-only examples. Password sign-up stays disabled.
4. Invited users enter through the local `scripts/provision-user.ts` command, which invokes Better Auth's server-only `createUser` API without request headers. Roles are exactly `user` or `admin` and come from that command. No registration, recovery, email, impersonation, or admin-management endpoint is public.
5. Session checks read the database on every request and decode the result through the shared domain `Session` schema. Cookie caching is disabled. Expiration, sign-out, deleted sessions, and changed roles take effect on the next read. Missing credentials produce `null`. SDK failures produce `AuthError`, never an authenticated or empty successful fallback.
6. The origin is explicit, has no path or credentials, and uses HTTPS except for HTTP on localhost or an IP loopback address. HTTPS requires Secure cookies. All session cookies are HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax. Trusted origins contain only that origin. Forwarded host, protocol, and client-IP headers have no authority.
7. Better Auth owns retry-free credential verification and database-backed rate limiting. Password sign-in permits ten attempts per rolling minute; email-only sign-in permits twenty. With no verified client-IP source, Better Auth uses one shared per-path bucket, which survives restart. This intentionally limits all invited users together. No claim of per-account or per-client limits is made.
8. POST requests require the exact configured Origin, including before the user has a cookie. The adapter buffers at most 16 KiB with a five-second deadline before calling Better Auth. Effect interruption cancels the body reader, with one second allowed for reader cleanup. Oversized bodies return 413, slow bodies return 408, and unreadable bodies return 400. Better Auth and Kysely Promise APIs are the SDK boundary. Local operations are uninterruptible until their Promise settles because these APIs do not cancel SQLite queries or password hashing. Scope cleanup cannot close the database while an admitted SDK operation is still running. The server owns bounded shutdown. There are no model calls, telemetry events, or application retries.
9. The database file has mode 0600 and its dedicated parent directory has mode 0700. Session tokens, passwords, and secrets never enter application logs or CLI output. Provisioning errors print a fixed message. The CLI requires `AMUSEME_ORIGIN`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `AMUSEME_DATA_DIR`, `AMUSEME_INVITE_EMAIL`, `AMUSEME_INVITE_NAME`, `AMUSEME_INVITE_PASSWORD`, and `AMUSEME_INVITE_ROLE`. ## Look and feel

The October 31 redesign was chosen after three independent design reviews (conversion-focused page design, interface polish and motion, and art direction). It is built for middle-school through college students and researchers:

- Nothing in the product reads smaller than 12px; body text and buttons are 16px, and every target is at least 44px.
- Plain words replace pipeline terms ("Clean copy", "What changed", "Describe the pictures"). Researcher detail stays one click away.
- Honesty labels are readable chips. AI-written content is always marked in violet; sample and illustrative content in blue; issues in amber; failure in red.
- The processing card's illustrated page shows the product's job: scrambled text, a broken equation, and a missing picture are fixed one step at a time. In the empty state, the same page sits beside the upload button as an example of copy-paste damage.
- The reader uses a system book serif for reading and Geist for everything else.

The October 31 redesign was checked in Chrome the same day: every state in both themes at desktop, 390px, and 320px widths, with no text under 12px, no control under 44px, no sideways scrolling, and no KaTeX or script errors. Sample playback and downloads were not re-run on the redesign; the browser observations below describe the previous layout.

## Three new directions

[`concepts/`](concepts/) holds three alternatives to the dashboard. Open [the concept index](http://127.0.0.1:4177/concepts/) from the same server. Each concept changes what the user does, not only how it looks:

- **Live Page** (`live-page.html`): the original pages show while processing runs, so reading starts at once. When the run succeeds, the clean copy takes their place at the spot being read. A switch at the top of the page then flips between the clean copy and the original pages, keeping the reading spot. A failed run leaves the originals and no clean copy.
- **Side by Side** (`side-by-side.html`): the original page beside the clean copy. Every part the AI rewrote is an "AI edit", sorted into edits that change words or symbols, edits that change only formatting, and parts missing from the clean copy. A circled-i button after the filters explains the marks. Clicking a marked part opens what it said before, what it says now, where it is on the page, and why. The AI saves no reasons, so "why" says so and points to the original instead of guessing. Small symbol changes, such as bold lost from a math symbol, are named outright.
- **Pieces** (`pieces.html`): the result as cards to take one at a time: an equation as LaTeX, a table for a spreadsheet, a figure with its description. Pieces appear only when processing succeeds. Table 1, printed across two pages, is one piece with both parts kept separate. Copying everything stays one click away.

The concepts share `concepts/shared/`: the saved sample (generated from this page's embedded data and `sample/processing-report.json`), one block renderer, and a reviewer strip. Live Page and Side by Side also use the first-read text and page positions (`sample-source.js`, see below) and rendered images of the two source pages. The strip switches between Empty, Working, Done, With issue, and Failed, and between light and dark. State and theme are kept in the URL. The same twelve-second timeline, illustrative issue (Equation 10), and real downloads apply to each. Progress shows only what a real run reports: the step, and for some steps how many pages or pictures are done. A chosen local PDF is labelled not processed.

`sample-source.js` was generated from the saved run's first-read ("joined") response for the sample paper. Two parts of it are hand-made: the map of first-read blocks that the clean copy folded into a neighbouring part, and the three places missing from the saved clean copy (the panel label "(b) Directed network", section 9, References, and the footnote at the bottom of page 2). The scripts that generated the two sample files are not in this repository. All 37 recorded changes land in either the 26 changed parts (24 marked by block in the dashboard, plus two headings) or those missing places.

These behaviours need real-app support that does not exist yet:

- Cancel needs a cancellation route; the application has none.
- Outlines and the kept reading spot need page boxes for every block. The saved run has them; extraction that gives text blocks only a page does not.
- Tables cannot be joined. Pieces groups a "(continued)" table by its caption, which holds for this sample only.
- Finding parts missing from the clean copy needs a comparison of first-read and clean text.
- Try again and a named failed page should show only when the failure is marked retryable and names a page.

Each concept was checked in Chrome at desktop width and in 390px and 320px frames, in both themes and every state. No text was under 12px, no control under 44px, and nothing scrolled sideways. There were no KaTeX or console errors. Copy all text in Live Page matched `sample/normalized.txt` byte for byte. Pieces copied an equation as LaTeX and two pieces together correctly. Downloads were not triggered; their links point at the sample files above. Drag-and-drop from the operating system and clipboard failure were not exercised. Real processing takes minutes, not twelve seconds; the timeline is for review only.
